fable: Encapsulation is a pick-one but most editors have both frames and subgraphs; coded the reusable form (subgraph) unless the sample named only backdrops/groups.

encapsulation is pick-one but most editors have both frames and subgraphs (Substance, ComfyUI since 2025); feedback's None competes with an empty array; Inline parameter controls needs a rule for control objects that are their own nodes (Max, Pure Data, Grasshopper); Drag from a port should say it means adding a node, not drawing an edge; edge style is hard to recall reliably for tools with a straight-versus-curved preference.
opus: Semantics forced one label onto tools that are two things at once: Node-RED and Make are message dataflow in mechanism and automation in purpose, and ComfyUI is dataflow that happens to carry models. Encapsulation also makes frames and subgraphs exclusive when most professional graphs have both (Nuke backdrops plus groups, Substance frames plus graph instances), so the code records whichever the sample's screen leads with.

Edge routing is the weakest sub-dimension here: it asks about a rendering detail that raters recall differently, and I changed two cells on the strength of two other recollections rather than my own. Arrangement's Free placement and Snap to grid are not exclusive — nearly every one of these editors snaps to a grid by default while letting you put nodes anywhere — so the pick one forces a false choice. Encapsulation has no member for a control-flow container that nests steps without being a frame or a subgraph (Power Automate's Scope, Condition and Apply-to-each), and Node content has no member for the portless automation step card, which is what my Step summary proposal is for.
sonnet: Add-by and feedback were often not visible in the one-line sample note; left empty rather than guessed where the product doesn't have a well-known, distinguishing behaviour I could recall confidently.

Content's Live preview needs its gloss tightened: it should mean an automatic thumbnail rendered on the node itself (ComfyUI, ShaderGraph), not a single shared viewer panel that can be pointed at any node (Nuke, Fusion) — I conflated the two for three instances in round 1. Encapsulation's four values don't cleanly cover a workflow tool whose only structure is condition/loop containers holding a linear list of steps (Zapier, Power Automate): it's not a subgraph-as-node, not a reusable function, and Frames undersells that the containers are structural rather than a loose visual annotation — I resolved it to Flat graph by elimination, but this is a real gap worth a closer look.

fable: Automation is a pick-one over pro NLEs that now ship captions and text-based editing; coded Manual for them and the automation only where it is the editor's headline.

automation is pick-one but pro NLEs now ship captions, filler removal and text-based editing, so the gloss must say whether it means the headline automation or the most the editor does; the Manual example (classic NLEs) suggests headline. nesting wants pick any, since Linked audio and video is true of every NLE alongside nesting or groups. The representation list has no value for keyframe and automation rows, which is most of a motion or audio timeline. Phone-editor zoom and marker features are hard to recall reliably.
opus: The entry assumes clips of media on tracks, so motion-graphics and DAW timelines fit only partly: their rows carry keyframes and automation, which representation cannot name. Operations is also a capability list rather than a mode list, which loses what Pro Tools makes explicit — that ripple and slip are exclusive edit modes there and simultaneous tools elsewhere.

Automation is pick one over values that are no longer exclusive: every NLE in this sample now ships speech-to-text captioning, so Manual has quietly emptied out and the code depends entirely on whether the sampler named captions on the screen — which is the rule I used, here and in the parent entry. Nesting has the same shape: Linked audio and video is glossed 'All NLEs', so coding it truthfully would swamp every other value; I reserved it for cases where two separate objects are actually tied together, which is why the phone editors are Flat. Ripple is also underdetermined — a gapless strip ripples by construction without ever naming the operation, which is most of the split on the mobile editors.
sonnet: Operations was often empty because mobile/simple editors expose trim handles rather than the professional blade/ripple/slip vocabulary the codebook names.

I systematically under-coded operations and navigation almost everywhere in this entry, missing baseline facts like blade/split, timeline zoom and markers, because I picked the single most distinctive operation per product instead of checking the whole pick-any list against what I actually know. One recurring codebook-adjacent tension: professional NLEs (Premiere, Final Cut, Resolve, Canva) now ship real auto-caption/transcription features, but they live in a separate panel from the base cut-clips-on-a-track timeline; I've held automation at Manual for these to describe the timeline's own default mode, distinct from Reels/TikTok-style tools where auto-captioning is squarely part of the one editing surface being sampled — automation may want a way to say 'this exists, but elsewhere in the app.'

Structure mixes what the person sees (a log) with architecture (a loop, a DAG); Single tool loop only discriminates if read as one tool looped. Approvals is pick one but Cursor, Windsurf and Zapier hold a per-class gate and a review at once, and Policy-based auto-approve overlaps Approve only destructive steps whenever the person writes the policy. Lifecycle bundles duration with unattendedness. Withdrew +Approve at milestones for opus's sharper +Approve the plan.
opus: Approvals and control overlap (Pause for approval restates whichever approval variation applies) and neither can express a milestone check-in where the agent asks whether it is on track (Replit). Structure was coded Plan then execute only where the plan exists as its own artifact, since almost every agent now keeps some todo list; lifecycle conflates duration with attendance, so a Deep Research run that streams a trace for ten minutes but survives you leaving had to be called a background job.

Two codebook faults drove most of this entry: `structure` mixes presentation with control flow, so Linear trace (a chat-style log) and Single tool loop (one action space) are true of the same agent at once and a pick one forces a coin flip; and `lifecycle` mixes duration with attendance, so a five-minute unattended run has no home between Minutes with live trace and Long-running background job. `approvals` has no variation for a gate that is neither per-tool nor final — hence two proposals, which are distinct: Approve the plan is a single pre-execution gate, Approve at milestones is a recurring checkpoint.
sonnet: Approvals was hardest: several products gate on milestones or an upfront plan rather than on destructiveness or a final diff, which the five listed variations don't cleanly cover (marked '?' once).

fable: Commit for multi-step applications straddles Explicit submit and Draft, then publish; I used Draft, then publish whenever progress persists across sessions before a final submit. Voice instances have no real prefill or validation timing; coded Empty/On submit by analogy.

commit is the codebook's fault: every save-and-return application (7 cells) is Explicit submit by its final button and Draft, then publish by its persistence, and the gloss does not say which wins; timing has no value for input that is never checked, so raters split n/a / +None / On leaving a field; One question at a time overlaps Multi-step for one-thing-per-page flows.
opus: commit was the hardest: most of these autosave progress between steps yet only commit the data at a terminal Submit/Pay/File, and I coded the terminal action except where nothing but continuous saving exists (Notion, Excel, System Settings). Voice instances stretch the timing sub-dimension — a spoken readback is confirmation, not validation, so 16 is n/a.

commit's Explicit submit and Draft, then publish overlap for every resumable application — the sibling form entry naming Job applications under Save draft settles it toward the draft reading, but the archetype gloss says publish, which no applicant does; organization conflates pacing with structure, so GOV.UK is truthfully both Multi-step and One question at a time and that sub-dimension wants to be pick any; timing had no way to say nothing is checked until +None.
sonnet: Voice instances (15, 16) got timing=n/a: field-based validation timing doesn't map cleanly onto turn-based conversational confirmation, which I judged unobservable-by-design rather than a knowledge gap.

Several pick-one cases held a product that truthfully spans two values (HealthCare.gov and Common App's prefill: Empty for a first pass vs. Autofill from a profile for a renewal/later college) — prefill wants to be pick-any, or the codebook needs a rule for 'first use vs. returning use'. Separately, several organization disagreements (Shopify, macOS, Salesforce) turned on whether headed tabs/section groups on a single page count as Sections or One page — the gloss should say explicitly that a headed sub-grouping is Sections even without full page breaks.

fable: Prefill lacks the commonest case, the product's own profile, so I proposed it; timing lacks a no-validation option, which utility forms need. Single-row field pairs (expiry/CVV, first/last) were still coded Single column.

columns: one rater coded every paired row (first/last, expiry/CVC) as Multiple columns, so the gloss should say a shared row inside a one-column form is still Single column; timing has no None and a live password meter makes While typing true beside On submit for the rest of the form, so it wants pick any or a which-check-wins rule; prefill lacks the product's own profile, which all three raters proposed under different names; commit is ambiguous about whether the unit is one page or the whole application.
opus: prefill is the weak sub-dimension: Browser autofill is the only external source named, so every product that fills from your own account profile (LinkedIn, MyChart, Zocdoc) or from a records lookup (GEICO) has nowhere to go. grouping also collides with the wizard entry — for long applications I coded the page-splitting I can see, since Split across pages is offered here.

columns caused a seventh of the disagreement on its own: the codebook does not say whether two fields sharing a row (first/last, expiry/CVC, city/state/ZIP) make a form multi-column, and it should — Multiple columns means a form laid out in columns of fields, not a paired row. timing mixes when (submit/blur/typing) with how (Asynchronous check), so a username check is both; grouping mixes visual grouping with pagination, so any wizard-shaped form is both Sections with headings and Split across pages and that sub-dimension wants to be pick any. errors needs a value for a complaint that arrives as the next conversational turn.
sonnet: Pick-one timing forces a choice between simultaneous checks (e.g. while-typing password rules and async username checks in the same account-creation form); I picked the more architecturally central one and named the other in the note rather than guessing a second sub-dimension.

prefill keeps forcing a pick-one choice where a product truly has both a blank baseline and a profile/records-based fill for returning users or later steps (instances 8, 9, 16, 20) — it wants to be pick-any, or the codebook needs an explicit 'first use vs. returning use' convention. fable: Assistance and cells depend on tier and licence (Copilot, AI fields); I coded what the product offers a paying user in 2026 rather than what one budget file uses, since the file is imaginary. Numbers' canvas is neither a free grid nor tables in one.

The entry does not say whether a sub is coded by what the sampled sheet shows or by what the product can do: cells, views and assistance ask what a cell or grid can hold or do, encoding asks how values are made visible, and I coded encoding by capability in round 1, which is most of my disagreement; structure conflates the container (canvas or document) with the structure imposed on the grid (typed records), so Coda truthfully holds two values.
opus: cells and encoding I coded from what that sheet shows; structure, views, concurrency and assistance from what the product affords on that surface, since no rater can know whether one particular budget froze its header row. Value-bound colour (a status or select option that is always green) I did not count as Conditional formatting, which I kept for rules a person writes — this is the cell most likely to split the three of us. concurrency is pick-one but real-time co-editing and comments coexist nearly everywhere; I took the stronger.

Nearly every disagreement here is one unstated rule: whether a cell answers for the sheet on screen or for what the product affords. The glosses actually settle it — cells asks what a cell CAN hold and views how the grid CAN be looked at (affordance), while encoding asks how values ARE made visible (this sheet) — and saying so would remove most of these cells. Two further gaps: encoding does not distinguish rules a person writes from colour that comes bound to a chosen option (every status column), and assistance cannot describe a model that fills cells as a column type rather than as a fill command.
sonnet: Concurrency is pick-one but several tools show both real-time cursors and comment threads at once (Sheets, Smartsheet); I coded the more architecturally defining mode (real-time co-editing) and named the secondary comments layer in the note rather than picking arbitrarily. For screens with no collaborator cues I fell back to product-family defaults (cloud-native tools = real-time co-editing, classic desktop-file tools = single-user file) rather than treating a quiet note as evidence of a solo file.

I was systematically under-listing pick-any sub-dimensions (cells, encoding, views, assistance) in round 1 — defaulting to the minimal set I could personally verify rather than the fuller feature sets these products actually ship, which is most of the disagreement here rather than genuine conflict. Separately, 'structure' doesn't have a place for a table's container (embedded in a document/canvas vs. a dedicated sheet file) — that's a real, recurring fact (Numbers, Coda, Quip) that's orthogonal to how typed the grid itself is, and forcing it into the same pick-one sub-dimension as Free grid/Typed records produces exactly this kind of disagreement.

fable: Fixed linear vs Branching is a matter of degree: almost every setup flow has one branch, so I coded Branching whenever an answer changes which screens come next.

review wants pick any for checkouts (a running total beside a final summary with change links); Grouped questions versus Whole sections has no threshold; Interview that fills steps overlaps presentation Conversational when the wizard is itself the conversation; presentation has no value for a standalone dialog window.
opus: sequence forced a judgment call everywhere: nearly every real flow varies a little on earlier answers, so I reserved Branching for flows where a whole section appears or disappears and left Fixed linear for ones whose steps are the same every time. presentation has no variation for an installer or setup assistant that owns its own window — I coded those Full page rather than Modal. review conflates reviewing your answers with previewing the result (Airbnb).

review wants to be pick any: a checkout truthfully has both a running order-total summary and a final summary with change links, and nothing in the codebook says which wins. Two further gaps: presentation has no variation for a wizard that owns a window of its own (installers, OS setup assistants), so they all land on Modal or Full page by force; and assistance's Interview that fills steps overlaps presentation's Conversational, so a chat intake gets counted twice unless the interview is read as something separate that fills an otherwise ordinary form.
sonnet: Resume was the hardest to pin down for consumer flows that don't advertise it (auto insurance quotes, brokerage signup): absent a known save-and-resume feature I defaulted to One sitting rather than guess Automatic/Save-and-return, which may undercount actual resumability.

Two codebook findings recurred: (1) 'sequence' Branching vs Task list get confused when a product both varies content by answer AND shows a resumable left rail of named parts (Stripe) — Task list's gloss is really about order flexibility, not about a named/resumable rail, and I'd been conflating the two. (2) 'assistance' Interview that fills steps overlaps with 'presentation' Conversational — for a chatbot intake, coding assistance as Interview-that-fills-steps just restates the modality rather than answering whether the system recommends specific values.

fable: source is the hard one: catalogue and place search is neither prefix-on-a-fixed-list nor popular queries; I used Prefix match for index lookups, Popular queries for popularity-ranked catalogues, Personal history when recents/saved dominate.

types has no value for entities without images, which is why places, addresses and code symbols each drew a proposal; source conflates matching (prefix) with ranking (popularity) so catalogue search splits raters; freedom's Free text allowed and Creates new values overlap for recipient fields where free text becomes a chip.
opus: types is the sub-dimension that breaks: it was written for pick-a-thing autocompletes and cannot express a continuation of the person's own writing (Smart Compose, Copilot, QuickType) or a code symbol, which is a third of this sample. source is also coarse — nearly every list is a prefix match over a set that is then ranked by popularity or by your history, and pick-one forces a choice between the matching and the ranking.

types is the sub-dimension that breaks: it has no type for a continuation of the person's own writing, for a code symbol, or for a place/address, and those are half this sample; source is pick one but every list is a prefix match over a set ranked by popularity or history, so it forces a choice between the matching and the ranking and should be pick any; freedom's 'Free text allowed' and 'Creates new values' overlap for chip fields like Gmail and Outlook.
sonnet: The 'types' dimension reads as built for search/communication inputs; generative ghost-text tools (Smart Compose, Copilot, fish, QuickType) and code-editor IntelliSense both needed proposals because none of the five listed categories describe what they suggest.

Two systematic misses recurred: (1) I was under-crediting 'accept' by Arrow keys wherever a suggestion list exists — treating arrow-to-highlight and Enter/Click-to-commit as two separate acts rather than crediting the arrow key as part of how a suggestion gets accepted, which both other raters counted consistently. (2) 'types' has no variation for geocoded places/addresses (map, travel and checkout autocompletes) — Query completions, Entities with images and Recent inputs all get stretched to cover it; +Places and addresses, proposed independently by a peer across five instances, names the real gap. Separately, 'freedom' for recipient-chip fields (email To fields) is ambiguous between Free text allowed and Creates new values — the codebook's own Creates new values example (tag inputs) is a better mechanistic match than the majority vote landed on.

fable: Ranked order has a cardinality but no form; proposed Sortable list. Timing for selects that reshape a form (country) or update a running total was coded by the visible effect, not the final submit.
opus: I read Label only strictly (nothing but the label) so it never co-occurs with the richer variations. Timing needed a rule: Immediately where the choice acts on the product itself with no confirm, On submit where it is data waiting on a button, and Previewed only for genuine live preview on hover (Word), not for options that merely picture themselves (Appearance thumbnails) — that line is the likeliest disagreement. largeSets is n/a for switches, which have no set at all.

fable: Model is pick-one but most pickers show several models at once; I coded the one shown first. Target does not apply to palette generators (Adobe Color, Coolors).

model conflates the selector's colour model with the readout format, so Figma (HSB square, hex box) splits raters; target has no value for paint programs that colour the brush rather than an object; Named tokens is read as design-system variables by two raters and as any theme-bound name by me.
opus: model is the sub-dimension that does not survive contact: several pickers express a colour in four models at once behind a toggle (Photoshop, the macOS panel, DevTools, GIMP), so pick-one records the default rather than the design, and palettes that never show a value (Reminders) have no model at all. I followed the codebook's exemplars where it names a product (Figma HSB, DevTools OKLCH) even when the default on screen is hex, and said so per instance. target also has no room for a tool colour or for a tool that colours nothing (Adobe Color, Coolors).

model is pick one but the serious pickers (Photoshop, GIMP, macOS, PowerPoint) show three or four models at once, so the code records the codebook's list order rather than the product; it also has no subtractive space (all three of us proposed CMYK) and its OKLCH variation is really the name of one product's format toggle, which drags DevTools' code. target has no value for a colour that is loaded into a tool (four instances here) and none for a picker whose output is applied to nothing at all, which pushed two of us to n/a. helpers is a list of choosing aids and cannot hold an import affordance like Slack's paste-a-theme line.
sonnet: Multi-tab/multi-model pickers (macOS Colors panel, Photoshop, GIMP, Adobe Color) force a pick-one choice among several simultaneously offered forms or models; I coded the most prominent/first-listed one each time rather than the full set, which likely undercounts real variety.

Codebook findings: (1) 'target' has no value for paint-style tools that load a colour into a brush/tool for future strokes rather than recolouring an existing object or selection — this recurred identically across four raster tools (Photoshop, Procreate, Paint, GIMP), which the adopted proposal now names. (2) 'helpers' Recent colours doesn't distinguish an auto-tracked recency list from manually-saved custom swatches (MS Paint) — both get forced into the same value. (3) 'helpers' has no room for a bulk paste-a-whole-theme mechanism (Slack); I now think that's rightly out of scope for a per-colour-choice helper list rather than a missing variation.

fable: Locale is unobservable from product knowledge for most web products; I coded it only for OS pickers and products whose settings I know, and ? otherwise.

annotations needs a rule for pickers with no day grid (n/a) versus a grid that marks nothing (None); presentation does not say where a large anchored panel (Airbnb) falls between popover and inline; selection cannot hold a recurring rule.
opus: The line between Calendar popover and Inline calendar had to be drawn by hand: I took popover to mean a small overlay anchored to a field and dismissed on pick, and inline to mean the calendar is the laid-out content of the sheet, panel or page. Several pickers also span two presentations at once (iOS Calendar: a month grid for the date, wheels for the time), which pick-one cannot hold. locale is close to unobservable — I coded week start and date format for products that ship internationally and left it empty for US-only services, which is an inference, not an observation.

selection has no value for a repetition — Todoist's 'every friday' produces a rule, not a date — and it is pick one although pickers like iOS Calendar and MyChart truthfully hold a date and a time chosen on the same surface; presentation mixes two axes (floating vs in the page flow, opened vs always visible) so Airbnb-style expanding panels can be coded either way; openBy has no honest value for a picker with nothing to open, which split us between n/a and Always visible, and annotations splits the same way between None and n/a when there is no day surface at all.
sonnet: Locale was mostly '?' by direct observation — I coded Week start/Date format wherever the product is a mainstream, internationally deployed consumer app with a standard grid, since that adaptation is real but usually invisible unless your own locale differs from the default; for single-locale government or internal-tool contexts I limited it to just Date format.

Two recurring corrections: (1) I was conflating 'has a date format at all' with 'adapts to the person's own locale' in the locale sub — several US-only or fixed-order services (GOV.UK DOB, Zocdoc, MyChart, Chase) got credited with Date format when both other raters correctly read them as not adapting to anyone. (2) 'selection' for date+time pickers with visually separate date and time controls (Google Calendar Android, Outlook) is ambiguous between Single date and Date and time depending on whether you're describing the whole task or just the calendar-grid control; I'm now reading it as the control being coded, which argues for Single date whenever the time lives in its own separate widget.

fable: Checks is nearly always Before upload from the outside: type and size are enforced on selection everywhere; After upload and Scanned are server behaviours a rater cannot see, so the sub-dimension barely discriminates.

checks conflates when a file is vetted (before or after) with whether it is scanned, so cloud drives split three ways; progress lacks an aggregate indicator, which two raters proposed independently; entry lacks the case where nothing is chosen at all.
opus: checks is the sub-dimension I trust least: what a service does after an upload (virus scanning, transcoding, quota) is invisible, so After upload is really where I could see no client-side refusal. preview is also pick-one where products mix — Gmail and ChatGPT show a name for a document and a thumbnail for an image in the same control.

sonnet: For cloud-storage products (Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) I coded checks as Scanned rather than After/Before upload, since their most distinctive, well-known check is backend malware scanning rather than a simple client-side gate — this may be under-crediting the size/type checks they also do before accepting a file.

Two recurring corrections: (1) 'checks' for cloud-storage uploaders (Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) kept pulling me toward 'Scanned' because these services are known for backend malware scanning — but that scanning is a separate, later feature (often only surfaced at download time), not the upload flow's own before/after check; the interactive check a person actually experiences during upload is a before-upload size/quota/name check in all three cases. (2) I was under-crediting 'entry' pick-any options (Paste, Drag-and-drop, Camera capture) across chat and composer apps where I'd only credited the primary Browse path — a systematic under-listing similar to other archetypes' pick-any sub-dimensions.

opus: commit is the sub-dimension that most often wants two values at once: Jira, Trello and several others accept Enter and offer tick/× buttons, and pick-one hides one of them. saved is nearly always Nothing, which makes it cheap agreement rather than informative; the interesting cases (a success toast in Salesforce, the (edited) tag in Slack) both had to be squeezed into Saved indicator, and no instance in this sample showed a conflict warning.
sonnet: 'Saved' was the hardest to code with confidence for enterprise tools I don't use daily (HubSpot, Trello, Todoist, GitHub) — I coded Nothing by default rather than assume a toast I can't clearly recall, which likely undercounts real saved-state feedback in those products.

fable: Visibility for feedback that goes to a company (ChatGPT, Teams, Zoom) is neither a private preference nor a public review; I used Aggregate only for telemetry and Private preference when it tunes your own experience.

context lacks the reason-tag case that two raters proposed independently; visibility has no value for feedback sent to the maker and never shown (ChatGPT, Teams, Zoom), so raters split Private preference / Aggregate only.
opus: visibility has no variation for feedback that goes to the maker and is never shown back to anyone (ChatGPT, Teams, Zoom); I coded those Aggregate only, which overstates how public they are. context also cannot hold the circumstance questions TripAdvisor asks (when you went, who with) or system-supplied context like Steam's hours played.

visibility has no value for a rating that goes only to the maker of the product — not published, not shown back, not averaged anywhere a person can see — which split us between Private preference and Aggregate only on ChatGPT, Zoom and Teams; context's Aspect ratings cannot distinguish facets of one thing (Airbnb's cleanliness/location) from separate targets rated in one flow (DoorDash's courier, restaurant and items); moment mixes 'the system asks you now' with 'it is tied to something you completed', which is what made Amazon and TripAdvisor look like after-completion ratings.
sonnet: Moment for algorithmic/system-triggered prompts (App Store review sheet) didn't fit On demand or After completion cleanly since neither the person nor a just-finished task triggers it — I used Periodic survey as the closest of the three, but it's a genuine edge case the dimension doesn't name precisely.

Two systematic misses: (1) 'context' has no place for post-score compliment/reason chips (Uber, Lyft, ChatGPT, Teams, Zoom) — I'd defaulted to Rating only or stretched Aspect ratings for a fixed-vocabulary tag list that is neither; two peers independently proposed near-identical variations for the same five instances. (2) 'visibility' — I was treating 'not shown to a counterpart' as equivalent to Private preference, when the sharper test is whether the score personalizes something for the rater (Private preference) versus pools into a metric a third party (admins, a public average) sees instead (Aggregate only); I had this backwards for IMDb, the App Store prompt, Teams and Zoom.

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

fable: Instances 14 and 19 bundle several sliders; I coded one of them each and said which. Scale is rarely knowable from the outside beyond the obvious (dB, price steps).

labels and precision overlap when the paired number boxes are also the value readout; Custom breakpoints needs a rule for an open-ended top bucket on an otherwise linear track; the unit of analysis is one slider, so a screen with two (Tinder) needs the sampler to say which.
opus: scale is close to unobservable: a person cannot see whether a volume or price track is linear, so I coded Linear where the mapping looks proportional, Logarithmic only where the units say so (dB, Hz) and Custom breakpoints for price filters whose last bucket is an and-up. precision also lacks the scrubby-number drag (Photoshop's label) that design tools all use, and Drag only I read strictly as no other route in.

precision's Drag only is an exclusive claim ('the only way in') sitting in a pick-any list, so one rater read it as a value that can be added to others and two of us read it as one that cannot — it should be phrased as 'No other route' or the sub should be pick one; the list also had no scrubby-number drag until sonnet's Scrub the label, which every design tool ships. scale is close to unobservable and cannot say which axis it describes (Spotify's log frequency spacing versus each fader's gain). labels does not distinguish an end label printed on the track from a number box that reads back the current value, which is where three raters split on every price filter.
sonnet: Two instances (14 Tinder, 19 Spotify) actually bundle more than one physical slider under a single sample entry; I picked the more distinguishing control to code and named the other in the note rather than inventing a compound value.

Two systematic errors: (1) I was treating 'Drag only' as compatible with other precision methods and adding it alongside Arrow keys/Paired number field in nearly every cell, when the codebook's own gloss and both other raters read it as exclusive by definition — if any other method works, the control isn't drag-only. (2) 'labels' Minimum and maximum conflates two different real UI patterns across the four price-range filters in this sample: some (Airbnb, Zillow) show only an editable min/max box pair, which belongs under precision's Paired number field instead; others (Amazon) show a separate passive printed span alongside a distinct editable box-and-Go control, where Minimum and maximum as a label is correct; and Booking.com has no editable boxes at all, only a passive Current value span. Treating all four as the same shape was the source of most of this archetype's disagreement.

fable: Semicolon (Outlook) and space (GitHub) were coded as Comma since the variation is really 'a delimiter key'; the name is narrower than the thing.

token: one rater never codes Text, so the gloss should say whether Text is implied by every chip; overflow lacks the stacked-rows case; vocabulary is unclear on a recipient field where an unknown email is accepted as an invitation.
opus: vocabulary needed a rule: Free creation where typing and committing simply makes the value, Create with confirmation where a new value is offered as an explicit Create row to choose, Existing values only where a typed string that matches nothing cannot be committed. Recipient fields sit awkwardly in that scheme — an unknown email address is both free creation and an invitation. The create list also has no variation for space as a separator (GitHub topics) and the entry has nowhere to record a cap on the number of tokens, which four of these impose.

create mixes the keystroke with the source: when a 'Create X' row is highlighted, Enter and Choosing a suggestion are the same action, which is where the three of us split on Linear, Notion and Airtable; token's Text reads as mutually exclusive with Avatar and Colour to one rater although every token in this sample shows text; overflow is pick one but describes two different states of the same field (Gmail and iOS Mail wrap while focused and collapse to a count when they are not), and it had no value for tokens that leave the field and become rows.
sonnet: Vocabulary was the hardest pick-one for enterprise label/tag fields that both suggest existing values and let you create new ones with a confirm step (Linear, Notion, Airtable, Jira, Asana) — I coded Create with confirmation only where a distinct 'Create X' affordance is part of the pattern, and Free creation where a new value seems to land without that extra step, but I can't fully verify the Jira/Asana distinction from memory.

One systematic miss dominated this archetype: 'token' content is pick-any, but I was coding it as if only one kind of content could be true per chip, picking Avatar or Colour alone whenever either was present and dropping Text even though nearly every chip in the sample also shows the value's name as text. This alone accounted for the bulk of the disagreement here. Separately, 'create' pick-any suffered a milder version of the same under-listing — I'd often credit only the one or two mechanisms my own note happened to describe rather than the fuller set both other raters independently confirmed.

On submit: Airbnb — Phone number at sign up

Specialized keyboard: Airbnb — Phone number at sign up

fable: validation has no On submit variation although the form entry does; five fields needed it.

validation omits On submit, the commonest timing, which two raters proposed with the same name; Prefix or suffix needs to say whether a decorative glyph counts or only an affix with content or a control; inputType has no value for obscured entry.
opus: The validation list is missing On submit, which the form entry has and which is what most real fields do; that gap alone forced four proposals' worth of codes. supporting treats the label as one of several optional parts, which makes Label almost universal and therefore uninformative, and it cannot record that a field has no label at all except by its absence. style also has no variation for a field drawn as a plain row in a grouped list, which is what most mobile settings fields are.

The validation list's missing On submit is the single biggest fault in this entry — all three raters hit it, two of us named it identically, and the third recorded that On leaving the field was only the nearest available fit. Two smaller ones confirmed by this round: supporting has no rule for what counts as a Prefix or suffix, so an icon inside a search box is an affix to one rater and nothing to another, while Clear button gets its own name — the sub should either name every affix control (clear, reveal, unit, menu) or none. And style's Outlined/Filled pair is Material's distinction; it cannot describe a white field on dark chrome (Amazon) or a Fluent field with a focus underline (Windows), which is both style disagreements here.
sonnet: This dimension has no 'On submit' validation-timing value, unlike the enter-data/form entries; for fields that visibly error only once you try to advance (GOV.UK, Google sign-in, Shopify phone, Amazon ZIP) I coded On leaving the field as the nearest of the four available options rather than force a mismatched one.

Two real codebook gaps and one systematic miss: (1) 'validation' has no On-submit value at the field level even though the sibling 'form' archetype does — a real, recurring omission both other raters independently named across five instances. (2) 'inputType' has no way to name password-style character obscuring, which is a genuine adaptation-to-content-type behaviour like the other three values, just for concealment rather than formatting. (3) I was under-crediting 'Label' across plainly labelled fields (passwords, bios, form questions) — a milder version of the pick-any under-listing seen in other archetypes, here on a dimension I'd treated as needing a visually distinctive label rather than any named prompt at all.

opus: scaleBehaviour needed a rule: every vector basemap both zooms continuously and changes what it draws, so I coded geographic maps Semantic zoom throughout and reserved Continuous zoom for canvases and 3D scenes where the representation never changes. moveBy has no value for physical movement, which is most of what navigation means in AR and XR.
sonnet: Corrected an initial instinct to code standard web/mobile maps as 'Semantic zoom' — the codebook itself cites Google Maps under 'Discrete zoom levels', so all tile-based consumer maps (Google/Apple Maps, Uber, Strava, Zillow, Citymapper, Windy) were coded Discrete zoom levels for consistency.

fable: modelLoading is largely unobservable from product knowledge; I inferred it from viewer technology (poster images on commerce sites, streaming in CAD and Matterport) and it should be treated as low confidence.
opus: viewerChrome has no value for a configurator's options rail, so Tesla, Porsche and Nike went under Side BOM + view with a note; it is the cell I would expect to split. modelLoading is also largely invisible from product knowledge — I inferred Progressive LOD and Streamed tiles from what the products must do with large assemblies and scans rather than from something the interface says.
sonnet: sceneGuidance was 'Free explore' for nearly every instance except the two tools that explicitly name guided or curated tours (Sketchfab-adjacent Smithsonian Voyager); most product/commerce/CAD viewers don't describe any directed attention mechanism.

Three real problems. (1) appearanceModes has no term between Realistic materials and Wireframe: molecular ribbons and plain grey CAD shading both get coded as 'realistic' for want of anywhere else — two raters independently proposed a variation for it (opus's Abstract representation, fable's Representation styles), so it is variation-worthy. (2) cameraControls has no term for phone AR, where the device is the camera; two raters proposed one here too, and the same gap shows up in the archetype entry under a third name (Move your body), so the codebook should settle on one. (3) 'Single download then view' and 'Placeholder then enhance' overlap badly — nearly every web viewer shows a poster while the asset downloads, which is why this sub split four ways across the commerce instances. sceneGuidance is also pick-one but conflates the default mode with an available capability, which split every CAD and science viewer between Free explore and Assisted find a part.

Resale marketplaces (SeatGeek, StubHub, Vivid) sell listings by section and row, so 'Click seats to toggle' does not apply to them.
opus: seatConstraints is mostly invisible: anti-orphan and contiguity rules only announce themselves when you break them, so outside Ticketmaster and Broadway houses I coded only what the interface states and left the rest off rather than guessing. Airline and rail maps also stretch seatHold — nothing is held and nothing is released either; the seat is simply assigned when you confirm, which Release on navigate away only half describes.
sonnet: sectionSummary was a frequent judgment call for airline seat maps, which mostly show per-seat prices rather than a single section-level figure; coded No section aggregate in those cases rather than force-fitting one of the other three.

Four findings. (1) 'Max quantity' is true of all twenty instances — every ticketing flow caps the order — so it discriminates nothing and is really a property of the archetype rather than a variation. (2) seatHold conflates two questions: whether the seats are held with a countdown and whether checkout has a timer. Airline and rail flows have neither (I had wrongly coded them all as timed holds), and 'Queue before map' is a different axis again, since a waiting room precedes the map rather than describing what happens to a pick. (3) sectionSummary is pick one but real maps do two of these at once — Ticketmaster and MLB both grey sold-out sections and print a lowest price — and neither covers a computed value score, which two raters independently proposed. (4) 'Grey unavailable' names a visual rather than a concept: American crosses seats out and Emirates dims them, and both are the same idea; 'Tier colours' and 'Heat of remaining' likewise blur on resale maps, where one colour ramp carries both price and scarcity.

fable: canvasMode is pick-one but FigJam, Miro, Mural and Lucidspark serve both authoring and facilitation; I coded by what the sample's screen description emphasises. lod is unobservable from memory for the smaller note-canvas tools (Heptabase).
opus: lod is hard to observe honestly: Constant detail versus Thumbnailify when small depends on a rendering threshold most people never notice, and I coded it from how each product behaves on a crowded board rather than from anything stated. canvasStructure also forced a single answer where two are true — Miro and FigJam both have frames and free placement — so I coded the structure the product enforces rather than the one it offers.
sonnet: canvasMode split on whether meeting/workshop tools (MS Whiteboard, Zoom Whiteboard) count as Facilitation just for being used live in a meeting; coded Authoring for those two since no explicit facilitator feature (timer, voting, spotlight) was named in the sample, unlike FigJam/Conceptboard/Lucidspark/Canva/Mural where one was.

Two pick-one sub-dimensions are mis-specified. canvasStructure should be pick any: a FigJam or Miro board is free placement, frames-as-regions and a connector graph simultaneously, and forcing one answer is what split us on FigJam. canvasMode describes a session rather than a screen — the same Miro board is authoring on Tuesday and facilitation on Wednesday, and Microsoft Whiteboard and Zoom Whiteboard split three ways purely on whether 'it lives in a meeting' counts — so it needs either a rule that only in-canvas apparatus (timers, voting) makes it facilitation, or to become pick any; opus's +Guided path is a genuine fifth mode for Prezi either way. Two smaller ones: canvasNav names desktop input devices (hand tool, middle-drag, scroll wheel), so touch-first canvases like Freeform and Muse have no literal match and every rater read them generously in a different place; and the Semantic zoom variation cites Muse for behaviour that only ever appeared in demos, while the shipped product is Frame as portal.

fable: Placement and Guide as pick-one strain on systems that combine a checklist, coach marks and a help menu (Notion, Slack, Asana); I coded the dominant surface. Adapts to demonstrated skill is only knowable for products that visibly test (Duolingo).

The entry does not say whether a guided flow (TurboTax's interview, Cash App's sign-up) is itself the guidance or only the help around it, and the three raters split on that unit. placement has no value for a full-screen card or a live call. guide and adaptation want pick any: Intercom is human and AI, Figma is by role and skippable.
opus: guide is pick-one but the four values stack in every serious product: a checklist (static) sits beside an assistant (AI) beside a chat (human), and I coded whoever does the actual teaching. The Static content versus Interactive walkthrough line is the one I expect raters to split on — I reserved Interactive walkthrough for systems where the real action advances the guidance (Slack's checklist, Photoshop's Discover, Duolingo) and coded pointer tours with Next buttons as static, which puts Canva on the other side of a line Miro-like tours usually sit on. adaptation is mostly Same for everyone because role questions are rare outside SaaS sign-up; 'Adapts to demonstrated skill' only fired for Duolingo and for a human doing the adapting. placement is pick-one over systems that use three surfaces at once, so it records the spine of the system rather than the whole of it.

`adaptation` is pick one but products routinely hold two of its values at once (Figma is both skippable and role-branched), and it has no value for a path that branches on the person's data rather than their expertise, which is what TurboTax actually does. The `progression` boundary between Disclosure over time and Just in time only also needs the gloss to say that disclosure means a paced plan, not merely tips arriving at intervals.
sonnet: placement is the hardest sub to apply when a guidance system spans several channels at once (a live call plus in-app hints in Superhuman; a checklist widget plus overlay pointers in Slack): coded to the most distinctive single mechanism per instance rather than left blank, with the tension noted.

Two codebook problems. (1) I repeatedly conflated `trigger` (what brings help up) with `progression` (how it proceeds once started) and with `placement` (where it sits) for the same instance — TurboTax and Photoshop both show this: coding a tutorial's internal linear steps under trigger and its on-demand invocation under progression. The three subs would benefit from a worked example that separates all three for one instance. (2) `adaptation`'s By role doesn't name situational branching driven by the person's own data (TurboTax's tax facts) as opposed to a self-reported category (a role question at sign-up); both are 'not the same for everyone' but only one is really a role.

relevance lacks a whole-product value, which every help menu and shortcut sheet needs; the other raters put those under Page, so the sub splits on a gap, not a reading. placement has no phone form of the popover (a bottom sheet) and no inline value. All three raters proposed the inline placement and the hover access under different names.
opus: proactivity is On request for 18 of 20, which is the honest finding: shipping products almost never volunteer help, and 'Suggested when stuck' — the variation that would matter most — went unused across the whole sample. relevance is nearly binary between Field and Page; 'The person's current state' only fires where an assistant can read the account, and it will be the value that grows as copilots spread. placement's four values cannot tell a popover from a bottom sheet, which is the same component on two form factors. The access and content subs disagree with each other about shortcut sheets, which is what the second proposal fixes.

Four gaps in this entry were found independently by all three raters, which is the strongest signal in the packet: help summoned by the control itself, a shortcut list as content, permanently inline help text, and help that is scoped to the whole product. The placement gap was proposed under three different names, which is the codebook's problem to settle. `placement` is also written for desktop — a mobile bottom sheet is field-scoped in intent but an overlay in form, and raters split on which to record.
sonnet: content has no variation for a plain keyboard-shortcut list (12, 13), since Shortcut sheet is only named as an access mechanism in this codebook, not as a content type; left empty rather than forced into Step instructions.

The `relevance` sub is missing a value between Field and Page on the broad end: a global, page-blind help search (macOS Help menu, Word's Help pane, Figma's/Notion's ? menu) returns the same thing no matter where you are, which is not what 'Page' names (a page-scoped result) — fable's +Whole product across six instances names a real, recurring gap, not a one-off. Separately, `access` needs a value for help triggered by interacting with the explained object itself (hover or a modifier-click) rather than a distinct help affordance beside it — opus's +The control itself is the cleaner statement of this than either fable's or my own narrower +Hover, since it also covers modifier-click cases that aren't literally hovering.

fable: Recovery lacks values for no-results pages that offer alternatives rather than a clear-filters button, and for access-denied pages.

recovery has no value for the commonest no-results page, where the way out is a new query; content has no value for suggested real items, so they land under Templates or samples. starters and recovery want pick any where a page offers both a template and an AI starter, or both new keywords and clearing filters.
opus: The entry is written for first-use and retail no-results screens, and the two proposals on recovery are where it runs out: a search with no matches usually needs a new query, not a filter reset, and a permission wall needs a human. starters is where empty states are quietly changing — four instances offer recommended real items rather than templates or samples, and 'Generated from a prompt' appears only as one option among four in Notion's new page. content's Create action is doing two jobs, since in several instances the only 'content' of the empty state is a button; cause was the easiest sub in my whole slice, with no ambiguity anywhere in the sample.

The entry's real fault is that `starters` and `recovery` were written for first-use emptiness and then applied to no-results screens: a nearby-homes strip is neither a template nor a recovery button, and 'None' cannot distinguish a page that offers nothing from one whose only way out is typing a different query. `content` also needs the gloss to say whether a control that is always on the screen (Add task, New Reminder) counts as the empty state's create action — that single question split all three of us across four instances.
sonnet: No-results screens whose only offered path forward is textual advice (check spelling, try different keywords) with no Clear-filters/Create/Import button are coded recovery None rather than forced into Clear filters, even when a related-search link is present.

The `starters` (pick one) and `recovery` (pick one) subs both lack a value for the single most common no-results pattern in the sample: offering real substitute items (nearby homes, related titles, other songs) instead of a template/sample/prompt-generated head start, and offering a better query instead of a filter to clear. All three raters independently reached for new language here across multiple instances, which is a strong signal these are missing variations rather than one-off product quirks — I adopted opus's two proposals since they were the ones applied consistently across the whole cluster (4/5/13/16 and 10/12/13/17) rather than per-instance.

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

recorded.gloss: The bubble states the value of the mark under the pointer — series, category, date, number — rather than naming or explaining a control; the entry's own sampling frame includes data charts but its content values are all about controls

fable: Placement lacks Below, the common case for top toolbars (seven of twenty). Timing mixes appearance delay with lifetime; most tooltips are both delayed and until-the-pointer-leaves, and I coded whichever the product makes salient.
opus: placement needed the largest proposal in my slice: 'Below' is the default for every top toolbar and is simply missing, so eight instances had nowhere to go; I used Auto-flip only for components that genuinely choose a side. content is written for controls even though the sampling frame names data charts, so four chart datatips needed a value of their own. timing mixes how long the tooltip waits before appearing with what makes it go, which is why Delayed and 'Until the pointer leaves' are not really alternatives — I read Delayed as 'a perceptible pause first' and 'Until the pointer leaves' as 'appears promptly and persists'. trigger's Keyboard focus is nearly unobservable without testing; I coded it where the product is known to implement accessible tooltips and left it off elsewhere, which is the least reliable column here.
sonnet: placement is the sub-dimension the four variations fit worst: Above is named but its mirror case, a tooltip below the target, has no equivalent, and it's at least as common (six of twenty instances here), hence the +Below proposal.

questions: Can one attention model span every app a person uses?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

fable: Trackers of one order or shipment show state on the object's own page, which none of the five surfaces names; timing is a pick-one but most products mix real-time events with threshold rules.

surface cannot say whether an ordinary push notification is an Interruptive alert or a Notification list, which is most of the disagreement here; it also has no variation for delivery out to another channel (email, Slack, SMS, SNS), so monitoring tools that page get Interruptive alert by default. granularity cannot tell a monitor's own scope from the objects under it. definition is pick one but banking apps hold a default and a person-set threshold at once.
opus: Granularity was the hardest: for alerting tools the monitored unit is the rule/series, which reads as Per object, while Per group vs Global health only separates cleanly when a public status page rolls services up. Severity is None for every consumer instance, so the dimension only discriminates among operations tools.

Two codebook problems. Surfaces has no line between a push banner and the list it lands in, so raters split the same product between Interruptive alert and Notification list; the gloss should say that the push is the interruptive surface and Notification list means a list you go back to. And 'definition' and 'severity' are pick one over products that truthfully hold two values (Monzo defaults plus budgets; Better Stack colour plus escalation).
sonnet: Signal and surface read as pick-any in practice for most consumer products (a push channel plus a persistent list/tile); definition is often blended (system default plus person-tunable threshold) and I picked the more distinguishing one per product.

Surface's Interruptive alert (glossed only as 'Critical alerts') and Notification list both plausibly describe an ordinary push before it settles into a list; that reading split fable+me from opus on almost every push-based instance.

entries.definition: A time-ordered record of what happened to an object or account, and who did it.

dimensions.name: Event detail

values.name: Erase the record
values.description: Entries can be deleted from the log — removing the record (and sometimes the content it refers to) rather than restoring, reverting or replaying anything; the characteristic action of personal-data activity logs

wild.note: Filtering by actor or type is common; the representation is fixed.

techniques.name: Log as an overview

entries.sample: Issue trackers, document tools, admin consoles and personal data dashboards.
usage: Logs are read only when something has gone wrong
questions: What is the right overview of history: events, versions or people?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

A workspace: Google Workspace Admin — Audit and investigation log

Filterable table: Google Workspace Admin — Audit and investigation log

fable: Delete-my-record (My Activity, Facebook, Dropbox on non-deletions) is neither read-only nor restore; coded Read-only since the past is not changed.

detail's Expandable groups overlaps aggregation's Consecutive edits collapsed. presentation mixes shape (timeline, table) with placement (sidebar in a detail view). actions has no value for deleting entries, and Replay's gloss means playback when re-delivery is what products offer.
opus: Presentation forces a choice between shape (timeline, table) and location (sidebar), so master-detail logs like GitHub Desktop fit badly; detail is also unstable for logs whose rows are one-liners but whose expansion is a full record or diff (CloudTrail, Stripe, Confluence).

`actions` is where this entry breaks: personal-data logs let you delete the record and API logs let you re-deliver an event, and neither is Read-only, Restore, Revert or Replay. `aggregation` also forces pick one over logs that both collapse runs and merge comments.
sonnet: Subject was the cleanest sub-dimension to apply; detail sometimes spans two variations (e.g., a table that also shows diffs) and I picked the more central one.

Aggregation keeps producing entries that are genuinely two things at once (collapsed-by-person AND merged-with-comments for Notion; day-grouped AND edit-collapsed for Dropbox) — it reads like it wants to be pick-any rather than pick-one. Detail also gets confused with aggregation when a pattern nests entries into expandable groups: that's about how entries are bundled, not how much one entry says once you open it.

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

Maps: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report
Categorical charts: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report

Strategic decisions: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report

Free-form canvas: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report

Dense wall: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report

Cross-filtering: Power BI — Sales and Marketing sample report

fable: Purpose applied by product family (analytics/BI → Strategic, monitoring/OS → Operational, personal health/finance → Motivation and learning); Density's Adaptive overlaps the other two, used for responsive card grids that reflow.

purpose is read from the viewer, not the screen, and the codebook dropped Sarikaya's Tactical genre, which is where analytics products fall. density's Adaptive is a layout property, not a density, and the scale has no middle between a few tiles and a wall. linking asks how widgets affect each other, but the entry's Drill-down component has no sub-dimension, so tap-for-detail has nowhere to go. refresh's Static snapshot means a frozen export and most web dashboards load on visit. ownership is a role on the folder, not a property of the dashboard.
opus: Refresh needed a fourth variation (see +On visit): most web dashboards are neither exports nor auto-refreshing. Purpose follows Sarikaya, which has no slot for personal decision support, so finance apps (Monarch, Robinhood, Coinbase) land in Motivation and learning by elimination; density conflates widget count with information density, which misfits single-table tools like Activity Monitor; I read Drill-through as any widget that opens a detail view of its own subject, and reserved Independent for dashboards where widgets neither filter each other nor lead anywhere.

Purpose is the worst cell here: the codebook keeps Sarikaya's strategic and operational poles but drops the tactical middle, so the analytics home of the person who runs a site (GA4, Vercel, Search Console, YouTube Studio) has nowhere honest to sit and the three of us spread across all four values. Density has the same missing middle — nothing between Apple Health's few tiles and a network operations wall — and Adaptive, read as 'responsive', would swallow every web dashboard. Linking was my error: its question is how widgets affect each other, and I had been coding plain tap-to-detail navigation as Drill-through.
sonnet: Alerting was mostly None for consumer/business dashboards; the two infra dashboards (Grafana, Datadog) coded as Threshold colours since the sampled panels weren't shown actively firing alerts.

Drill-through vs. ordinary tap-to-detail is under-specified: the gloss's own exemplar (Power BI drillthrough) is a destination page that inherits another visual's filter context, but a tile that just opens its own metric's history page (Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Robinhood, Coinbase, Task Manager) does neither that nor truly 'affect' another widget — I held Independent throughout rather than call plain navigation a form of linking. On visit and Categorical charts (and Control widgets) are real, repeated gaps in Refresh and Widget types, not one-off misreads; adopting opus's proposals for all three.

values.name: Read on view
values.description: The notification is never removed — opening the surface or the item only clears its unread state, and the entry stays in the list until it ages out; the default in social and activity feeds, and distinct from an explicit Dismiss or Done

dimensions.question: What does a notification show?

wild.note: Per-app settings and focus modes exist; conditions and rules rarely do.

examples.note: Filter by reason and custom filters

techniques.name: Reason filters
techniques.how: Filter by why a notification exists, then turn any filter into a rule for what arrives in future.

techniques.name: Summaries with sources
techniques.how: Stacks collapse into a summary whose every line opens the notification it came from.

entries.sample: Mobile operating systems, developer platforms, social and SaaS products.
usage: Notification centres become a second, neglected inbox
questions: Should the notification centre and the inbox be the same overview?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

fable: Half the sample never removes a notification at all, which none of the four clearing variations covers; Grouping is hard when apps bundle by app inside chronological or priority sections.

clearing has no value for the commonest lifecycle, an item that never leaves and only loses its unread state; two raters proposed it under different names, so it wants to be a variation. filtering cannot say whether per-type settings that gate push but not the list count, and iOS holds Focus, Summaries and per-app toggles at once. grouping conflates ordering with bundling, so an inbox of task or issue rows in time order splits raters. bulk lists with Message-only-style contradictions aside, most bulk disagreement is omission.
opus: Clearing assumes a notification leaves, which half the sample never does (see +Read on view). Filtering is nearly degenerate — almost every product has per-type settings somewhere — so I coded Per-source toggles only where muting a specific source is a first-class, used control, and Everything where the surface shows all activity addressed to you; Snooze went unused because it is always a secondary option beside dismissing.

Clearing assumes a notification leaves; in half the sample it never does, and fable and I proposed the same missing variation under two names (I have taken fable's, Mark read). Filtering is close to degenerate — every product has per-type settings somewhere — so it only discriminates if Per-source toggles is read strictly as muting a named source (channel, repo, page, project) rather than as any notification setting.
sonnet: Clearing was the hardest sub-dimension: several consumer feeds (Instagram, LinkedIn) have no memorable explicit dismissal action beyond reading, coded '?'.

Two codebook-shaped findings: (1) filtering's Per-source toggles vs Everything split turns on whether a rater credits any settings screen that gates notification generation somewhere (per-type, per-channel, per-page) or requires proof that the specific SETTING changes THIS SPECIFIC surface as opposed to a separate push channel — the stricter reading converges on Everything far more often, and the codebook doesn't say which test to apply. (2) clearing has no value for the common case where a notification is never removed and merely loses its unread styling on view or on Mark all as read — fable's Mark read and opus's Read on view are independent proposals for the same real gap; I'm adopting Mark read as the name since some instances (Reddit, Facebook) trigger it via an explicit button rather than passive viewing.

dimensions.name: Stage model

dimensions.name: Stage detail

values.description: The current state is written out as a sentence or paragraph with no sequence drawn — no bar, timeline or map; the common government casework shape, where the wording carries everything

values.name: Narrative status text
values.description: The current stage is conveyed as a plain-language paragraph rather than a bar, timeline or map — typical of government casework portals

dimensions.name: Updates
dimensions.question: How does status reach the person?

dimensions.name: Exceptions
dimensions.question: What happens when progress stalls?

wild.note: People can choose notifications for some carriers; nothing else changes.

techniques.name: Pick my milestones
techniques.how: People choose which stage changes notify them, and where: lock screen, email or nothing.

techniques.name: Why is it late?
techniques.how: An explanation drawn from tracking events, with the options that are really available.

entries.sample: Retail, delivery, ride-hailing, travel and government casework.
usage: People check trackers compulsively when estimates are vague
questions: How should uncertainty in an estimate be shown?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

fable: Stage model is a pick-one over things that mix: food delivery is fixed stages drawn on a live map, flights are stages with estimates plus a moving aircraft; coded the structure (stages) not the drawing.

stages is a pick one over values that mix structure (fixed stages) with rendering (live location) and with a branch (exceptions), so every food tracker with a map and every carrier splits three ways; it wants to be structure only, with the map under presentation. exceptions cannot separate a status headline that says Delayed from a banner that explains why.
opus: Stages is the hardest cell: almost every tracker has both a fixed sequence and an estimate, so Fixed stages vs Stages with estimates turns on which the screen leads with, and Exception branches competes with the Exceptions dimension for the same evidence. Exceptions is also largely about a conditional state I am coding from memory of disruption, not from the screen the sample names.

Stages is the fault: every tracker has a sequence, most have an estimate, and carriers have exception statuses, so three of the four variations are true at once and the code turns on which one the screen leads with. Exception branches also competes with the exceptions sub-dimension for the same evidence — one of them should be dropped or renamed.
sonnet: Government casework trackers (USCIS, GOV.UK) don't fit any of the four presentation variations; proposed +Narrative status text. Exceptions was often Silent by default with no evidence of an explaining path for the everyday case.

I under-credited Stage names across most live/timestamped trackers (Uber, Lyft, UPS, USPS, United, Delta, FlightAware, DHL, Shop) — a systematic miss on my part, not a codebook problem: I was reading 'has timestamps/a map' as sufficient and forgetting that the timestamped events are also named. Separately, stages' Exception branches is glossed only as 'carrier tracking' with no sharper test for when a delay is a structural fork vs. just an exceptions-dimension banner on an otherwise fixed line — FedEx/USPS/DHL only converged once I anchored on 'this is literally the named example' rather than judging the structure independently.

entries.name: Badge
entries.definition: A small indicator on another element showing a count or a status.

dimensions.name: Meaning
dimensions.question: What does the badge say?

dimensions.name: Overflow
dimensions.question: How are large counts shown?

dimensions.name: What counts

values.name: Pending actions
values.description: The badge counts work waiting for the person — updates to install, apps to update, tasks to finish — rather than anything read, unread or addressed to them; the counting rules as written assume a message inbox

dimensions.name: Aggregation
dimensions.question: Does it roll up?

values.name: Device total
values.description: One indicator for every unread notification on the device, on system chrome rather than on any app's icon or nav entry (watch faces, always-on displays)

wild.note: Turning badges off is common; defining what counts sometimes is.

examples.name: iOS
examples.note: Badges on or off per app

techniques.name: Define what counts
techniques.how: A badge’s rule is an editable query, so the count means what the person needs it to mean.

entries.sample: Navigation surfaces across communication and productivity apps.
usage: Unbounded counts are ignored
questions: Are badge rules part of the attention budget or separate from it?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

fable: Overflow is unobservable from memory for most social badges (coded ?); Counting rule has no value for system-condition badges (updates), coded n/a; Aggregation read as Per item unless children carry their own badges that the parent sums.

aggregation cannot say whether a single list's count is Per item (the folder-count example) or Rolled up to parent (the items inside it), which is nearly all of the disagreement here; rule assumes a message inbox and has nothing for badges set by a system condition; overflow is unobservable from memory for most social badges.
opus: Overflow is often unobservable from product knowledge — you only learn the cap by accumulating a hundred unread items — so four cells are ?; I read Per item as a badge on a leaf (channel, label, chat), Rolled up to parent as a badge on a nav entry totalling a surface, and App icon total as the OS-level badge.

Aggregation is the split: fable reads Per item as 'each nav entry carries its own badge' and I read it as 'the badge sits on the leaf it counts', and the gloss (Folder counts / Account totals) does not say which question is being asked — where the badge sits, or how much it totals. Overflow stays partly uncodeable: you only learn a cap by accumulating a hundred unread items, so ? is a real answer and Capped is often a guess.
sonnet: Several hosts carry two badge types at once (a plain unread dot plus a mention count); pick-one forced me to choose the more informative/numbered variant and note the other. Rule sub-dimension didn't fit system-generated flags (software update pending, browser update overdue).

Overflow's 'Capped' vs '?' split across several consumer apps (Facebook, Instagram, X) is mostly a shared gap in what any of us could actually confirm having seen, not a real reading disagreement — worth flagging that these need a fresh look at the product rather than more reconciliation. Aggregation also needs a clearer line between 'several sibling items each keeping their own badge' (Per item) and 'several child items summed into one shown at a parent' (Rolled up to parent) — LinkedIn/Teams tripped this because each nav icon's own number is itself a sum of underlying events, which reads like a rollup even though the badges are Per item relative to each other.

fable: Severity coded by consequence and colour together (grey informative → Information, cannot send/save or yellow → Warning, red blocking → Critical); Link to fix had to stand in for links that only inform (status page).

action's Link to fix and Primary action are told apart by navigation in the codebook's examples but raters read them by button styling; action also has no value for a link that only informs. scope's Page example is account warnings, which reads as Whole app when scope is taken to mean what the condition concerns rather than what the banner governs.
opus: Severity had to be read from the condition rather than the styling — offline notices are drawn grey or neutral but genuinely impair the product, so I coded them Warning throughout; Link to fix vs Primary action I split on whether the control navigates to where the fix happens or performs it in place.

Two codebook faults. Scope asks what the condition applies to but its Page gloss ('Account warnings') pulls account-wide conditions onto the page they are shown on, so scope and placement answer the same question twice. And action has no value for a link that informs rather than remedies (GitHub's status page), which pushed two raters to code an information link as Link to fix.
sonnet: Scope between Whole app and Page was sometimes a judgment call for account-wide banners that only render at the top of whichever page loads; I used Whole app when the same condition follows the account across every page.

Action's biggest problem: 'Primary action' sounds like it should mean any prominent single CTA button, but its codebook example (Restart to update) is specifically an immediate, in-place fix, while 'Link to fix' 's own example (Update payment method) is exactly the kind of button — Update payment, Select a plan, Verify, Confirm — that navigates to a separate flow instead. I coded five different account-gating banners as Primary action in round 1 by pattern-matching 'button' rather than 'does it resolve in place or send you elsewhere', and only Windows 11's actual Restart-now button is the real Primary action case in this sample. Scope also needs a clearer rule for connectivity/offline banners: the strip's visual footprint (over one list, under one bar) undersells that losing the network is a whole-app condition.

dimensions.question: What does it look like?

dimensions.name: Delay handling
dimensions.question: When does it appear?

values.name: Moves to background
values.example: Export jobs that notify on completion

dimensions.name: Coverage
dimensions.question: What does it block?

dimensions.name: Control
dimensions.question: Can the work be stopped?

wild.note: Indicators are never customizable; reduced-motion settings sometimes affect them.

techniques.name: Send to background
techniques.how: Any long wait can be moved to a background tray that notifies on completion.

entries.sample: Loading, upload, export and installation flows.
usage: Indeterminate waits feel longer than determinate ones
questions: How should an AI agent’s progress be shown when its steps are not known in advance?

coding.protocol: Shared sample of recalled instances; three model raters coded independently; Fleiss’ κ per sub-dimension, item-weighted per entry; disagreements sent back for reconciliation; majority consensus.

Percentage: iOS App Store — App download ring

Circular determinate: iOS App Store — App download ring

Immediately: iOS App Store — App download ring

One control: iOS App Store — App download ring

Pause and resume: iOS App Store — App download ring

fable: Delay handling is unobservable from product knowledge (whether a spinner waits 300 ms cannot be recalled), so every instance is Immediately; Coverage has no value for indicators that block nothing but are not in a tray.

coverage asks what is blocked but has no value for an indicator that blocks nothing and sits outside a tray (a hairline over a feed, a word by a title), so those split three ways; determinacy is pick one over bars that show a percentage and a time estimate together; delay is unobservable from memory.
opus: Coverage reads as what the indicator blocks, so its fourth variation had to absorb everything non-blocking: real trays (Chrome, Drive), a menu bar item, an app-icon ring and an ambient saving chip all landed in Background task tray. Determinacy also hides a common hybrid — a bar that is really a fake curve (YouTube) versus one tracking bytes — which the codebook cannot separate.

Coverage is the fault line: its question ('what does it block?') and its variations ('background task tray', 'one control') answer two different questions — what is blocked and where the indicator lives — so every non-blocking indicator that is not literally a tray has nowhere honest to go.
sonnet: Form and determinacy sometimes both apply (a bar that is also inside a small control); picked whichever was the dominant visual described.

Coverage's line between 'A region' and 'Background task tray' is underspecified for modeless-but-separate-window cases (Finder/Explorer copy windows): the codebook glosses tray with Chrome downloads but doesn't say whether a whole floating window counts as a region or a tray. Also for coverage, a blocking modal dialog (Notion/Canva) needs its blocking behaviour, not its visual footprint, to decide Whole page vs A region — the gloss doesn't say this explicitly.
